jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description

GIS Analyst – ArcGIS, SQL & GIS Application Development

Position Overview

Support highly complex GIS applications while working across spatial data, GIS application development, database technologies, testing, and web/mobile applications. This role provides opportunities to work closely with development teams and Project Managers to improve GIS solutions, streamline spatial data needs, and support application quality, milestones, and deadlines.

The role will primarily support applications associated with environmental and natural-resource functions, with additional application development support assigned as needed.

What You'll Do / Key Responsibilities

Support multiple highly complex GIS applications.
Collaborate with development staff by providing advice and guidance as needed.
Work closely with Project Managers to ensure project quality, milestones, and deadlines are met.
Develop solutions and streamline spatial data needs through the maintenance and modification of existing web, client/server, or mobile applications.
Support additional application development needs as assigned.
Adhere to applicable technology and client standards.
Develop or approve plans for testing and implementation of web-based, client/server, mobile, or data system applications.
Evaluate the impact of new technology and recommend solutions to persistent problems.
Serve as a customer service liaison to the client and external consultants.
Maintain current knowledge of changing IT technologies through continuous learning.
Support applications across PC-based, web-based, and mobile platforms.
Support legacy application development and maintenance where applicable.

Required Qualifications

4 years of experience in GIS, cartography, CADD, or a related field.
4 years of experience developing user interfaces, menus, and macro-level commands, performing complex spatial analyses, and producing reports according to customer specifications.
Experience with ArcGIS Online (AGOL) and Portal.
Builder skills.
Dashboard skills.
4 years of experience assisting in the development of GIS that create, maintain, or leverage geospatial basemap information.
Experience creating basemaps and tile caches.
Experience with imagery analysis.
4 years of advanced SQL skills, including writing database scripts, stored procedures, functions, triggers, and SSIS packages.
Experience maintaining spatial databases, documenting procedures, validating data, and updating and maintaining metadata for new and existing items.
4 years of advanced skills in unit testing, system testing, regression testing, and automated testing to ensure product quality meets client expectations.
2 years of experience with C#.NET, VB.NET, ASP.NET, XML, AJAX, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Transact SQL (T-SQL), TypeScript, and Power Apps.
Knowledge of ADA Compliance with 1+ years of experience.
Bachelor's degree required. Foreign degrees will be accepted if evaluated as equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree.

Preferred Qualifications

1+ years of experience with MS ADO, GIT, MS Office, and Helix.
1+ years of experience with Angular.

Job Title:
GIS Specialist

Company:
Celerity

Location:
Remote (work from home eligible) West Coast based with occasional hybrid cadence for meetings and workshops within the San Francisco Bay Area, CA.

Job Type:
Hourly

About Celerity

Celerity is an agile risk optimization company that empowers public utility organizations by converting complex data into clear, actionable intelligence to mitigate risk, optimize assets, and maximize project results. Blending extensive client experience with deep vendor-side acumen, Celerity energy engineers orchestrate precision data analysis, strategic consulting, and project management services to solve complex energy challenges through acute listening, proactive thinking, and relentless grit. Learn more at consultcelerity.com.

Position Overview

The GIS Specialist supports Celerity’s project team by providing geospatial and data management expertise to client projects. This role is responsible for reviewing engineering documents, validating asset data, and using GIS tools to create, analyze, and maintain records and maps. Working closely with engineers and project managers, the GIS Specialist I helps ensure accurate documentation of utility assets, supports quality control processes, and contributes to client deliverables.

Key Responsibilities

Review engineering documents, drawings, and specifications to identify key information for analysis
Verify data on underground and overhead electric system structures, including components, configurations, and supporting documentation of current asset conditions
Perform searches and data validation using client platforms such as GIS, SAP, and document repositories
Conduct GIS functions including creating, modifying, and updating records, maps, and diagrams; querying geodatabases; and extracting data for analysis
Gather and research data from engineering as-built drawings and project documentation
Perform quality control (QC) and review checks for asset inventories, engineering drawings, and related records
Provide mark-ups and redlines on engineering documents in accordance with client and project specifications
Maintain project tracking logs and coordination tools, including status updates, schedules, and challenges
Produce project reports, maps, and updates as needed to support client and internal teams

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geography, Engineering, or a related discipline; OR a GIS certificate plus relevant experience
At least 1 year of work experience (GIS experience preferred but not required)
Demonstrated skill with Esri ArcGIS (ArcGIS Desktop 10.x/ArcGIS Pro) to develop, edit, and maintain data from engineering as-built drawings
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Access)
Understanding of geographic data types, including land base, imagery, and utility infrastructure
Strong attention to detail and ability to complete complex assignments accurately
Effective verbal and written communication skills; professional demeanor
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation to travel to client sites
Ability to work extended hours and/or overtime as needed

Physical Requirements

Ability to remain in a stationary position approximately 50% of the time
Ability to operate a computer, scanner, copier, and related office equipment on a regular basis
Must be able to communicate effectively with staff and clients to exchange accurate project information
Ability to move and/or carry boxes up to 40 pounds with or without assistance

The salary range for this position is provided in good faith and is subject to variation based on geographic location, candidate experience, and market conditions. Final compensation will be determined after a comprehensive evaluation of the candidate’s qualifications and alignment with the role.

In accordance with applicable pay transparency laws—including but not limited to those in California, Colorado, New York, Washington, and other jurisdictions—we disclose salary ranges to promote equity and transparency. Where required by law, compensation and benefits information will be included in job postings or made available upon request.

This job description outlines the primary responsibilities and standards of the position but is not exhaustive. Employees may be asked to perform additional duties that are reasonably related to their role and consistent with company policies and applicable labor laws.

Employee welfare and development is important to us, and we sponsor many activities outside of work to promote team building as well as sponsor formal training and certification. We are proud to offer a comprehensive health and welfare benefit package that includes:

jobs.title: Geospatial Engineering Surveyor
jobs.description:
About Castle Surveys

Castle Surveys is an independent, multidisciplinary geospatial and land surveying company, headquartered in Ashby de la Zouch with offices in Manchester, London, Cheltenham and Scotland. We deliver everything in-house, with no subcontracting, and work to an ISO 9001 aligned management system.
Our work is genuinely varied. On any given week the team might be scanning a listed building, mapping a motorway corridor, surveying a reservoir bed, tracing buried utilities or setting out a data centre floor. That variety is exactly what makes this a brilliant place to build a surveying career.

The role

We're looking for a Geospatial Engineering Surveyor to join our team. You'll be the person on site making sure the data is right: establishing control, carrying out topographic surveys, setting out, then processing it all back in the office and delivering clear, accurate results to our clients.
It's a hands on role with real responsibility. You'll work across construction, infrastructure, highways, utilities, heritage and development projects, sometimes as part of a team and sometimes leading small jobs yourself.
And it doesn't stop there. Once you've got the core skills nailed, we'll train you in our specialist areas, so the role can grow with you.

Key responsibilities

On site

Carry out topographic land surveys using total stations, GNSS and levels, capturing detail to the client's specification.
Establish and maintain survey control networks, including traverses, GNSS control and precise levelling, tied to OS National Grid and Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Set out for construction and engineering works, from site grids, piles and foundations to roads, drainage and structures.
Carry out as-built and monitoring surveys, and check work against design.
Use 3D laser scanners for measured building and structure surveys, [CONFIRM, e.g. Leica RTC360].
Plan your own site day: kit checks, calibration records, access and permits.

Back in the office

Process and adjust survey data, including control network adjustments and GNSS post processing.
Produce accurate 2D and 3D CAD drawings to Castle Surveys and client standards.
Write clear survey reports and control reports, including accuracy statements and QA records.
Check your own work and colleagues' work as part of our ISO 9001 aligned QA process.

Health, safety and clients

Work safely at all times, following RAMS, site rules and our Behavioural Safety Programme, and use your Stop Work Authority when needed.
Contribute to RAMS for your jobs.
Be the friendly, professional face of Castle Surveys on site, liaising with clients, site managers and engineers.
Look after company vehicles and survey equipment.

Where the role can take you

The core surveying skills are the foundation. Once you're confident with them, you can move into one or more of our specialist areas, with training provided.

Mobile mapping
Capturing highways, rail and urban corridors at road speed with vehicle mounted LiDAR and 360° imagery, then processing and extracting design ready data.

Drone (UAV) surveys
Planning and flying photogrammetry and LiDAR missions over sites, quarries, roofs and infrastructure
CAA flyer ID, GVC, and flight training under our Operations Manual

Hydrographic surveys
Bathymetric surveys of reservoirs, rivers, canals and harbours from our survey boats, including multibeam and single beam work

HP SitePrint robotic layout
Printing building layouts directly onto slabs and floors for contractors, including data centre and commercial fit out projects

What you'll need

Essential

At least [INSERT, e.g. 2] years' experience as a land, engineering or geospatial surveyor.
Confident with total stations, GNSS and levels on site.
Solid understanding of survey control, coordinate systems and survey accuracy.
Experience of setting out on construction or engineering sites.
Good working knowledge of CAD, ideally AutoCAD or Civil 3D, and survey processing software such as [INSERT, e.g. Leica Infinity, n4ce or LSS].
Clear, accurate written reports.
CSCS card, or willingness to get one.
Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel and stay away when a job needs it.
A careful, safety first attitude and pride in getting things right.

Desirable

A degree, HNC or HND in geomatics, surveying, civil engineering or similar.
Working towards, or holding, RICS or CICES chartered status.
Experience with 3D laser scanning and point cloud software, such as Leica Cyclone or Autodesk ReCap.
Any exposure to mobile mapping, drone surveys, hydrographic work or robotic layout.
Rail (PTS), highways or utility survey experience.
First aid or SSSTS qualifications.

What we offer

A competitive salary, depending on experience.
23 days' holiday plus bank holidays.
Company pool vehicle or allowance, fuel card,
Pension scheme.
Clear progression into specialist areas such as mobile mapping, drones, hydrographic surveying and HP SitePrint.
The latest kit, from Leica instruments and scanners to mobile mapping systems and survey vessels.
A friendly, owner led company where your work is noticed and your ideas are listened to.
Toil System

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note telling us about the surveys you've enjoyed most to info@castlesurveys.co.uk, with "Geospatial Engineering Surveyor" in the subject line.

Castle Surveys is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone, and we're happy to make reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process; just let us know.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems.

With general direction, this position is responsible for the development, administration and implementation of environmental programs in accordance with company and governmental requirements. Recommends and implements modifications to environmental program processes and procedures. Develops programs to ensure compliance with required federal, state and local agencies. Ensures records and documents are prepared, maintained and submitted to appropriate agencies. Represents the company as a spokesperson with external regulators, auditors and government representatives. This position involves the exercise of independent judgment and discretion about matters of significance.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Handle program management for defined areas, work more independently, and mentor EEs I.
Air Quality: Oversee air permit compliance and maintain records.
Prepare semi-annual compliance reports and emissions inventories (EIR).
Develop Health Risk Assessment (HRA) Prioritization Scores & collaborate with consultants.

Hazardous Materials:
Develop and maintain hazardous materials business plans (CERS).
Audit hazardous waste manifests for compliance.

Stormwater Management:
Conduct comprehensive stormwater monthly visual observations.
Coordinate inspections with D-Max Engineering/City of Poway.
Coordinate routine maintenance/service with SWIMS.
Lead SWPPP updates and implement corrective actions.

4.Industrial Wastewater:
Oversee sampling protocols and laboratory coordination.
Manage discharge monitoring reports (DMRs).
Support with inspections from the City of San Diego.

Pressure Vessels & Boilers:
Coordinate inspections with certified contractors.
Ensure compliance with ASME/NBIC standards.
Support Environmental Engineer III with scheduling as needed.

SPCC:
Monitor SPCC annual inspections and & provide training.
Coordinate with consultants for plan updates. PE Stamp Needed.
Assist with tank inspections and secondary containment checks.
Support High Desert Safety Engineers as needed.

DOT Compliance:
Conduct audits of hazardous material shipping procedures.
Lead training sessions for DOT compliance.

Generators:
Maintain inspection records and track maintenance logs.

Mentorship:
Train and oversee EEs I on basic tasks and regulatory requirements.

General:
Assist in preparing for internal and external audits.
Performing technical reviews of purchase requests, chemical orders, and safety data sheets.
Conducting inspections of stormwater best management practices, tanks, secondary containment, pressure vessels, boilers, and other environmental systems.
Supporting or leading internal and external environmental audits.
Managing hazardous-waste manifests and hazardous-material records.
Collecting wastewater samples, maintaining pH and flow records, and coordinating laboratory testing as needed.
Tracking air emissions and supporting emissions inventories, permit compliance, and required reports.
Maintaining environmental permits, plans, inspection schedules, training records, and corrective actions.
Work closely with Facilities, Engineering, Operations, Safety, contractors, consultants, and regulatory agencies.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals with diverse backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Qualifications

Typically requires education or formal training equivalent to the completion of a bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering or a related technical field and two or more years of related experience.
Additional professional experience may be substituted in lieu of education.
Must demonstrate a thorough understanding of environmental engineering principles, concepts, theories, regulations and practices and have extensive skills including organizing, planning, scheduling and coordinating workloads to meet established deadline or milestones.

Must possess:

The ability to analyze and resolve complex technical problems.
Strong verbal and written communication skills to accurately document, report and present findings.
Strong interpersonal skills to effectively interface with all levels of employees, senior management and outside representatives.
Strong computer skills.
The ability to work independently and in a team environment is essential as is the ability to work extended hours and travel as required.
The ability to obtain and maintain DoD security clearance is required.

jobs.title: Geospatial Data Scientist Lead
jobs.description:
The Company

We are NEURAL EARTH
. We bring clarity to physical risk, enabling leaders to engage with confidence and enact resilient, business-critical decisions. Today's environmental, economic, and infrastructure challenges are deeply interconnected, yet the data required to understand these relationships is scattered across siloed and aging systems. Neural Earth enables operational execution, delivering a single decision intelligence platform that unifies planetary, governmental, and asset-level data, always on and always learning. This is technical work that requires patience. It requires teams willing to operate at the intersection of AI research, geospatial science, distributed systems, and enterprise deployment. It is also incredibly rewarding. Join us at Neural Earth — the next frontier is here.

THE TEAM

Neural Earth's Science team transforms raw environmental data into intelligence that moves markets and protects lives. You will join a growing group of geospatial data scientists, ML specialists, and researchers led by a strong leader, who sets a high bar: the work must be publishable in quality and deployable in production. You will collaborate closely with Engineering, Product, and Revenue to make sure what we build in science reaches the customers who need it.

THE ROLE

This is a founding, staff-level role with a direct report. You will own Neural Earth's geospatial data science function, define the technical strategy for how we ingest, structure, and pipeline multi-hazard geospatial data, and make that data usable by our ML and AI teams to power quantified intelligence products used by insurers, government agencies, and infrastructure operators. You are comfortable across geospatial data broadly, not specialized in a single sub-discipline like meteorology. You work at the intersection of geospatial engineering, data infrastructure, and applied science. You do not stop at the paper. You build things that ship, scale, and make hazard data understandable to people who are not scientists. This is you!

How You'll Be Successful

Model: Design and deploy Python-based geospatial models that quantify environmental and physical hazards at a level of precision that drives real business decisions, not just research outputs.
Build: Architect Neural Earth's geospatial data pipelines from the ground up, including the systems, infrastructure, and scientific frameworks that turn raw hazard data into indexed intelligence products customers can act on. Structure and prepare that data so it is ready to run through the models our ML and AI teams build, and own the production pipelines that keep it flowing reliably.
Translate: Convert complex, multi-hazard scientific findings into business-ready products that are legible and compelling to insurance underwriters, government operators, and enterprise decision-makers.
Lead: Serve as Neural Earth's internal and external subject matter expert on geospatial data science, driving customer calls, proposals, and strategy discussions, while managing and developing a direct report.
Validate: Establish rigorous validation standards for all geospatial models, ensuring methods are reproducible, cross-validated, and defensible across industries and geographies.

WHY WE VALUE YOU

You have 5+ years of experience working with geospatial data broadly, across formats and hazard types, in a research or applied setting, in addition to any graduate degree.
You write Python fluently and have built production-grade geospatial models using GeoPandas, Rasterio, GDAL, xarray, and Shapely.
You know how to engineer and structure geospatial data so it is ready to feed ML and AI models built by others. You would rather apply and extend someone else's research five different ways than chase original research yourself.
You are fluent in geospatial data formats (GeoTIFF, COG, GeoParquet, NetCDF) and have worked with large-scale raster, vector, and time-series datasets in cloud environments.
You have shaped a scientific or technical framework, not just executed within someone else's.
You think in systems. When you see a wildfire burn scar, your mind goes to downstream snowpack risk.
You can walk a customer through a confidence interval in the morning and brief a C-suite on business implications in the afternoon, without ever sounding condescending or over your audience's head.
You define your own structure in ambiguous environments and build something real before the roadmap is written.
You do not ship unvalidated models. You have the judgment to know when something is ready.
You have mentored or managed at least one direct report or informally led technical work, and you know how to grow talent, not just do the work yourself.
You care when your hazard model shapes an insurance decision or informs a disaster response. This matters to you.

Requirements

Master's or PhD in Geospatial Science, Data Science, Atmospheric or Environmental Science, or a related field
5+ years of experience with geospatial data in a research or applied setting, outside of academic training
Prior experience in insurance, energy, government, defense, or climate tech
Demonstrated ability to build and lead a technical capability, including managing or mentoring at least one direct report

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $185,000 to $231,000 annually
, reflecting progression within the role based on demonstrated growth and impact.

At Neural Earth, we believe in pay equity, transparency, and rewarding growth. Our compensation philosophy is built on an equitable model with offers based on role, level, and expertise. This approach ensures that all employees are paid fairly and equitably without the influence of external factors like negotiation skills or previous pay history. This structure provides clarity, consistency, and alignment between pay, performance, and career development.

Benefits

At Neural Earth, taking care of our people isn't just something we strive for, it's who we are. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you at every stage, whether you're advancing your career, growing your family, or planning for the future. From day one, you'll have access to:

Competitive base compensation regardless of work location
Company performance-based cash bonuses
Majority employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents
Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO)
Group Life Insurance at 2x your base salary, paid by the company
FSA and HSA options to maximize your healthcare dollars

We know that when people feel supported, they can focus on what matters most at Neural Earth which is doing great work, growing in their careers, and making a meaningful impact.

jobs.title: Junior GIS Technician / GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
JOB OPPORTUNITY

Junior GIS Technician / GIS Analyst

Department: Information Technology / GIS

Reports To: GIS Manager/Public Works and Engineering Department

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt (Contract Position)

Location: Addison, Texas

Position Summary

The GIS Technician/Analyst supports the Town of Addison's Geographic Information Systems (GIS) program by maintaining, updating, analyzing, and distributing spatial data used by the Public Works and Engineering Department.
This position performs GIS database maintenance, map production, spatial analysis, application support, and field data collection using Trimble GPS equipment. The role includes both office and field work to ensure Town infrastructure assets are accurately mapped and maintained.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

GIS Data Management
• Maintain and update enterprise GIS databases and geodatabases.
• Edit and manage utility, transportation, stormwater, and other municipal GIS layers.
• Perform QA/QC to ensure data accuracy and consistency.
• Integrate data from as-built plans, surveys, engineering drawings, GPS field collection, and departmental records.
• Maintain GIS documentation, metadata, standards, and procedures.
Field Data Collection & GPS Operations
• Collect, verify, and update asset locations using Trimble GPS equipment and mobile GIS applications.
• Conduct field inventories of water, wastewater, stormwater, streets, traffic signs, and right-of-way infrastructure.
• Process, validate, and quality-check GPS data.
• Verify asset attributes and conditions during field inspections.
• Coordinate field activities with Public Works and Engineering staff.
• Maintain GPS equipment and field collection devices.
GIS Analysis & Mapping
• Create maps, exhibits, reports, dashboards, and visualizations.
• Perform spatial analysis to support planning, engineering, asset management, and operational decision-making.
• Produce map products for Town staff, management, Town Council, and public meetings.
GIS Application Support
• Support ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, and related GIS applications.
• Assist with the development and maintenance of web maps, dashboards, mobile applications, and field data collection tools.
• Support GIS integrations with Cityworks, Survey123, permitting systems, asset management systems, and other enterprise applications.
• Provide GIS support and training to Public Works and Engineering staff.
Project Support
• Participate in GIS implementation projects and special initiatives.
• Support asset inventory, infrastructure mapping, and capital improvement projects.
• Coordinate with consultants, contractors, engineers, and surveyors as needed.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of:

• GIS principles, practices, and spatial databases.
• GPS data collection methods and workflows.
• Municipal infrastructure and utility systems.
• Cartographic standards and map design.
• Coordinate systems, projections, and asset management concepts.

Proficiency with:

• ArcGIS Pro
• ArcGIS Enterprise
• ArcGIS Online
• Survey123
• Field Maps
• Trimble GPS equipment and software
• Microsoft Office Suite

Ability to:

• Collect accurate GPS data in the field.
• Interpret engineering plans, surveys, and as-built drawings.
• Analyze GIS and GPS data issues.
• Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical users.
• Work independently and manage multiple projects.
• Work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

Minimum Qualifications

GIS Technician
• Associate degree in GIS, Geography, Surveying, Computer Science, Engineering Technology, or related field.
• Two (2) years of GIS experience.
• Experience with ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and GPS/GNSS data collection.
• Valid Texas Driver's License.

GIS Analyst
• Bachelor's degree in GIS, Geography, Geospatial Science, Planning, Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.
• Three (3) years of progressively responsible GIS experience.
• Experience with enterprise GIS systems and spatial database management.
• Experience with Trimble GPS field data collection.
• Experience developing GIS applications, dashboards, and web maps.
• Valid Texas Driver's License.

Preferred Qualifications

• GISP certification.
• Esri technical certifications.
• Experience with ArcGIS Enterprise.
• Experience with Cityworks and municipal asset management systems.
• Experience with SQL Server and relational databases.
• Experience with Python, Arcade, or GIS automation.
• Knowledge of municipal utility and public works operations.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to walk, stand, bend, and perform field work for extended periods.
• Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
• Ability to lift and carry equipment up to 30 pounds.
• Ability to operate Town vehicles and travel throughout the Town.

Primary Technologies

• ArcGIS Enterprise
• ArcGIS Pro
• ArcGIS Online
• Field Maps
• Survey123
• Trimble GPS/GNSS Receivers
• Cityworks
• SQL Server
• Microsoft 365

This position plays a key role in maintaining accurate geospatial information that supports infrastructure management, asset inventory, planning, emergency response, and operational decision-making throughout the Public Works and Engineering Department.

jobs.description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Senior Environmental Engineer serves as a strategic technical leader responsible for the oversight and execution of environmental compliance, permitting, and sustainability programs. This role involves managing complex regulatory requirements at the local, state, and federal levels, specifically as they relate to mining, aggregates, asphalt, and building materials production.
You will act as a primary liaison between operations and regulatory agencies, ensuring that all sites within your district operate within the law while minimizing their environmental footprint. The position requires a high degree of independence, a proactive 'self-starter' mindset, and the ability to provide technical mentorship to junior staff and production teams.

KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Administer the full lifecycle of environmental permits (Air Quality, NPDES, Water Rights, US Army Corps, Wetlands, and Endangered Species).
Lead the development and implementation of critical environmental plans, including SWPPP (Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans) and SPCC (Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure).
Manage the timely submission of all regulatory reports, including Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs) and annual emissions inventories.
Build and maintain professional relationships with local, state, and federal regulators; represent the company at public hearings and permit actions.
Conduct regular site inspections and recordkeeping reviews to identify potential risks.
Provide hands-on guidance to Plant Managers and Production staff on best practices for water discharge, oil storage, and waste management.
Serve as a technical lead for environmental incidents, ensuring proper reporting, remediation, and root-cause analysis.
Assist in property acquisitions and divestitures by managing Phase I/II environmental investigations and overseeing remediation contractors.
Coordinate with land management teams to ensure mining reclamation activities meet permit requirements and long-term sustainability goals.
Identify and implement innovative engineering solutions to improve air/water quality and reduce resource consumption.
Develop and deliver environmental training programs for site personnel to foster a culture of shared responsibility.
Actively promote and adhere to Martin Marietta’s world-class safety standards, ensuring all environmental activities are performed without risk to personnel.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, or a related STEM field.
Work Experience

5+ years of experience in Environmental Compliance, preferably within the Aggregates, Mining, or Heavy Construction Industries.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Critical thinking
Problem solving
OSHA/MSHA compliance and regulations
Environmental engineering
Environmental risk
EPA
Technical aptitude (AutoCAD, GIS, Microsoft Office Suite)
Time management
Detail oriented

Leadership
Effective communicator (written and spoken)

Strong hand-eye-foot coordination is essential. You must have good depth perception with or without seeing aid for distances up to 150 feet.

All duties require outside assignments and require periods of work in all weather conditions, cold, wet, dry, and dusty ;Must be able to work in areas where noise levels are up to 85 dbs.

jobs.title: Quality Control Manager - Federal Environmental Remediation Program
jobs.description:
Description

At Weston Solutions, Inc. you will do meaningful work and make valuable contributions. Employee ownership at Weston is a path to professional growth and access to diverse opportunities in a highly connected community that works together across key service areas to make a difference in the environment. Weston has continued to evolve and adapt to our changing world as a premier provider of environmental and infrastructure services for over sixty years. In both the public and private sectors, our teams help identify, solve, mitigate, and manage critical environmental issues to help clients achieve a more sustainable future.

Weston Solutions, Inc. is seeking a Quality Control Manager (QCM) to support a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) environmental remediation construction project. This position will be responsible for implementing and managing the project Quality Control Program during excavation, remediation, transportation, and disposal activities associated with contaminated soil. The QCM will serve as the primary quality representative on site, ensuring compliance with contract requirements, project specifications, safety standards, environmental regulations, and Weston quality procedures. The successful candidate will work closely with project management, field personnel, subcontractors, regulatory representatives, and government stakeholders to ensure project objectives are achieved safely, efficiently, and in compliance with all quality requirements.

Location:
The project is in East Helena, MT. Candidates may relocate or support the work on per diem. Fieldwork for this project will shut down during the winter. Travel will likely be required during the winter months to support other projects.

Expected Outcomes:

Manage and implement the project-specific Quality Control Plan in accordance with USACE requirements and project specifications.
Conduct daily quality control inspections of excavation, remediation, construction, and restoration activities to verify compliance with contract requirements.
Coordinate and document the Three Phases of Control process, including Preparatory Meetings, Initial Inspections, QC Inspections, and Follow-Up Inspections.
Maintain complete and accurate quality control documentation, including daily reports, inspection reports, deficiency logs, testing records, and project correspondence.
Coordinate with project management, field supervisors, environmental professionals, laboratories, and subcontractors to ensure all work is completed in accordance with approved plans and specifications.
Review and verify field sampling, excavation activities, soil management procedures, waste characterization, transportation, and disposal operations.
Monitor subcontractor performance and ensure corrective actions are implemented for identified deficiencies or quality issues.
Support environmental compliance requirements and ensure field activities adhere to project permits, regulatory requirements, and approved work plans.
Facilitate project meetings with clients, USACE representatives, subcontractors, and project personnel regarding quality requirements and project performance.
Assist with project planning, scheduling, reporting, and closeout activities to support successful project execution.
Ensure all testing, inspection, and documentation requirements are completed and submitted in a timely manner.
Support a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement throughout project execution.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, Engineering, Environmental Science, Geology, or related technical discipline preferred, with 3 to 5 years’ experience in environmental quality control management. Equivalent years of work experience will be considered in place of a B.S. degree.
Experience should include supporting federal construction, environmental remediation, hazardous waste, civil construction, earthwork, or excavation projects.
Three years’ experience supporting environmental remediation projects involving contaminated soil excavation, waste characterization, hazardous materials handling, and disposal operations preferred.
Experience serving as a Quality Control Manager, Quality Assurance Representative, Superintendent, or similar role on USACE, NAVFAC, DoD, or other federal projects.
Current USACE Construction Quality Management (CQM) for Contractor’s certification required or ability to obtain prior to project assignment.
Thorough understanding of USACE Resident Management System (RMS) Contractor Mode (CM) version 3.0, Patch 515, for the submittal of Daily Quality Control Reports (DQCRs), PWS submittals, and Official Requests for Information (RFI) and maintained on the Weston SharePoint with accessibility to the corps.
Thorough understanding of USACE quality control requirements, EM 385-1-1 standards, and federal construction contract administration.
Ability to read, interpret, and enforce project specifications, drawings, work plans, and contract documents.
OSHA 30-Hour Construction Safety training required.
Current First Aid/CPR certification required or ability to obtain upon hire.
40-Hour HAZWOPER with current 8-Hour Refresher required; may be obtained after hire if not currently held.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to interact effectively with clients, regulatory agencies, construction personnel, and subcontractors.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and project documentation software.
Working knowledge of Procore is preferred.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel extensively to project locations throughout the United States.
Ability to perform field work in varying weather conditions and terrain.
Must be able to lift and carry 50 pounds without assistance.

We fully invest in our people: Weston provides a generous, comprehensive benefits package program that offers employees high value options with solid financial protection, meeting the personal needs of its people and their families.

Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k) with base and matching employer stock contributions.
Paid time off includes personal, holiday, and parental leave.
Life and disability plans.
Critical illness and accident plans.
Work/Life flexibility.
Professional development and certification opportunities.
Employee Stock Ownership participation.
Career advancement opportunities supporting major federal environmental and infrastructure programs.

Compensation will vary based upon experience, education, skill level, certifications, project experience, and other compensable factors.

jobs.description:
Position: 
Supervisor, Environmental, Health & Safety and Quality

Employment Type: 
Full Time Permanent

Vacancy Status: 
Existing Vacancy

Location: 
Brampton, ON / Burlington, ON (Hybrid)

DCM is a leading Canadian tech-enabled provider of print and digital solutions that help simplify complex marketing communications and operations workflow. DCM serves over 2,500 clients including 70 of the 100 largest Canadian corporations and leading government agencies. Our core strength lies in delivering individualized services to our clients that simplify their communications, including customized printing, highly personalized marketing communications, campaign management, digital signage, and digital asset management. From omnichannel marketing campaigns to large-scale print and digital workflows, our goal is to make complex tasks surprisingly simple, allowing our clients to focus on what they do best.

The Role

As a Supervisor, Environmental, Health, Safety & Quality (EHSQ), you will lead the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of EHSQ systems across the organization. This role is responsible for ensuring compliance, driving continuous improvement across sites, and overseeing the ISO 9001 Quality Management System, along with supporting alignment with ISO 14001 (Environmental) and ISO 45001 (Health & Safety) frameworks.

This is a hybrid role, working a minimum of 2-3 days onsite per week. As this role will mainly be responsible for our Brampton and Burlington operations, you will be expected to split your onsite days between these two locations on a weekly basis. Collaboration across other DCM's Canadian locations, cross-functionally is also required.

Key Responsibilities

Own and maintain the ISO 9001 Quality Management System across multiple sites, ensuring compliance, audit readiness, and continuous improvement of quality processes

Manage Quality Incident Response (QIR) process and escalations and engage with customers on quality issues and corrective actions, ensuring to track and report quality KPIs and performance trends

Support internal auditor training and capability development

Maintain and improve Health & Safety Management System, ensuring compliance with Canadian legistlation

Lead incident investigations, root cause analyses, and corrective/preventive actions to improve workplace safety and reduce risk

Support injury management, ergonomic assessments and claims process and 

Monitor safety performance and recommend risk reduction initiatives

Maintain certification compliance, including FSC, MDEL, SGP, and SFI, and support audits across sites for certification requirements

Support alignment with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 best practices

Drive continuous improvement initiatives, standardize best practices across Canadian sites

Deliver training on EHSQ systems and compliance requirements

Provide reporting and insights on risk and trends to leadership and maintain business continuity and emergency response planning

Skills & Experiences

Post-secondary education in Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Quality, or related field (designation preferred), with 3–5 years working in a manufacturing or multi-site production environment 

Strong working knowledge of ISO 9001 is required, with familiarity of ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 an asset 

Understanding of Canadian health & safety and environmental regulations 

Experience supporting certification programs such as FSC, SGP, and SFI

Demonstrated experience leading incident investigations and implementing corrective actions

Knowledge of workers’ compensation and injury management 

Strong communication skills with ability to translate technical concepts to diverse audiences

Results-oriented mindset with a focus on KPIs, compliance, and continuous improvement

What we offer

Comprehensive healthcare, dental, and vision coverage for you and family

Company-matched pension program

Tuition reimbursement to invest in your growth and career development

Collaborative and supportive work environment where your ideas are valued and your impact is visible

Compensation

$65,149 - $81,436 CAD per year

The compensation range listed reflects the expected compensation for the role. Actual compensation will be determined based on individual skills and experience.

If you don’t meet every requirement listed above, we still encourage you to apply. We’re interested in the diverse experience, potential, and perspective you can bring to the team.

DATA Communications Management Corp. (DCM) is committed to equal employment opportunity, employs and does not discriminate against all qualified persons without regard to race, colour, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any other classification protected by applicable federal and provincial laws. Should you require any accommodation throughout the recruitment and selection process, please get in touch with us through the form at the bottom of the page (https://www.datacm.com/about-us/lifedcm/), so that we can ensure your equal participation.

jobs.title: Principal Consultant, Renewable Energy Land Use Planner
jobs.description:
Shape the Future of Clean Energy Development in the Pacific Northwest

ERM
is seeking a Principal Consultant, Renewable Energy Land Use Planner
in Portland, Oregon or Seattle, Washington
to help lead and expand our renewable energy permitting practice across the Pacific Northwest. In this highly visible role, you will guide complex permitting, environmental review, and land use planning efforts that support the development of utility-scale renewable energy and infrastructure projects, helping clients advance the clean energy transition while navigating regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations.

Why This Role Matters?

As renewable energy development accelerates throughout the Pacific Northwest, successful project delivery depends on thoughtful permitting strategies, regulatory expertise, and strong collaboration with agencies and stakeholders. In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor to clients, leading land use planning and permitting efforts that enable critical clean energy infrastructure projects to move forward efficiently and responsibly.

What Your Impact Is:

You will help clients successfully develop renewable energy and infrastructure projects by leading permitting strategies, preparing regulatory applications, evaluating land use requirements, and coordinating multidisciplinary teams. Your expertise will help identify permitting risks, develop practical solutions, and support sustainable project approvals throughout Oregon and Washington.

What You'll Bring:

Required

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Environmental Planning, Urban and Regional Planning, Environmental Science, Geography, Natural Resources, Public Policy, or a related field, or 12 years of equivalent experience.
6+ years of experience supporting permitting and land use planning efforts for renewable energy, transmission, infrastructure, or similar development projects.
Demonstrated experience preparing land use permit applications and supporting local government approval processes.
Experience conducting zoning analyses, code consistency evaluations, and preparing findings demonstrating compliance with local and state land use regulations.
Familiarity with Oregon land use planning requirements, including Oregon Statewide Planning Goals and county development codes.
Familiarity with Washington land use regulations, SEPA review processes, and local development permitting requirements.
Excellent technical writing, communication, and client management skills.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced consulting environment while managing multiple concurrent projects.
Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area.

Preferred

AICP certification.
Experience working directly with Oregon and Washington counties, States (EFSC, EFSEC), planning commissions, or local hearing bodies.
Experience obtaining Oregon and Washington wetland and waters permits, including permitting under State Removal-Fill programs, Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, and related state and federal regulatory frameworks.
Experience developing wetland, waters, and habitat mitigation strategies and coordinating with state and federal resource agencies to support renewable energy, transmission, and infrastructure projects.
Knowledge of Oregon Department of State Lands (DSL), Washington Department of Ecology, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and state and federal habitat mitigation requirements preferred.

Key Responsibilities:

Lead and support the development of permit strategies and entitlement pathways for environmental permitting and land use planning efforts associated with utility-scale solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS), wind energy, transmission, and other energy infrastructure projects throughout Oregon and Washington.
Lead preparation of county and municipal land use permit applications, including Conditional Use Permits and EFSC/EFSEC applications.
Coordinate with state agencies, counties, municipalities, and special districts to support permitting and regulatory compliance requirements.
Conduct detailed zoning and land use due diligence assessments for project sites.
Interpret local development codes, comprehensive plans, and applicable state land use requirements to identify permitting risks and opportunities.
Prepare code consistency analyses demonstrating project conformance with applicable code.
Evaluate local permitting pathways and jurisdiction-specific code requirements for renewable energy developments.
Develop findings of fact and permit application narratives supporting project approvals.
Support projects undergoing review through the Oregon Energy Facility Siting Council (EFSC) and Washington Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council (EFSEC) process, including preparation of application materials, Requests for Amendment, compliance reporting, and coordination with Oregon Department of Energy staff.
Coordinate with interdisciplinary project teams including biologists, wetland scientists, archaeologists, visual resources specialists, and other technical experts regarding technical studies and review environmental documentation prepared in support of permit applications.
Mentor junior and mid-level staff in environmental permitting, land use planning, and project management.
Provide technical review and quality assurance for permitting deliverables.
Contribute to development of best practices, tools, and methodologies for renewable energy permitting projects.

For the Principal Consultant, Renewable Energy Land Use Planner
position, the anticipated annual base pay is $100,600–$152,100 (USD)
. Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off (vacation, sick, and floating holidays), parental leave, medical, dental, vision, life, disability, AD&D insurance, 401(k), and other applicable benefits to eligible employees.

Who We Are:

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!

jobs.title: Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Title: Environmental Engineer (Mid-Level Project Manager)

Job Description

This mid-level Environmental Engineer role focuses on managing and supporting environmental remediation projects, including Phase I and Phase II site assessments and corrective actions, across multiple locations in Delaware. You will contribute to EPA-funded, recession-resistant projects while working closely with a small, collaborative team to deliver high-quality environmental engineering and geology solutions.

Responsibilities

Assist in overseeing and managing environmental projects from initial assessment through remediation, primarily within offices located in Milton and Newark, Delaware.
Manage and direct site evaluations under Delaware HSCA and Brownfields programs, as well as EPA Region III initiatives, starting from pre-remedial assessments.
Lead and coordinate Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments and remediation activities, ensuring compliance with applicable regulations and standards.
Conduct strategic project planning using a data quality objectives approach and develop focused planning documents that guide investigation and remediation activities.
Guide implementation and provide oversight of field work, including environmental media sampling, installation of appropriate tooling methods, and coordination of laboratory method selection.
Support the development of fully characterized soil and groundwater evaluations, integrating field data and laboratory results into comprehensive site models.
Perform data evaluations and statistical analyses to support site-specific risk assessments and inform remedial decision-making.
Develop and oversee implementation of geologic and hydrogeologic resource evaluations to understand subsurface conditions and contaminant behavior.
Perform detailed geologic and hydrogeologic reviews to evaluate site conditions, groundwater flow, and potential contaminant migration pathways.
Ensure environmental compliance across projects, including adherence to EPA Superfund and related regulatory requirements.
Collaborate with environmental scientists, geologists, and engineers to deliver integrated solutions for remediation, brownfield redevelopment, and corrective actions.
Communicate project findings, technical results, and recommendations clearly to internal team members and external stakeholders.

Essential Skills

35 years of experience in environmental engineering or geology, with direct involvement in remediation and site assessment projects.
Hands-on experience with Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments and remediation activities.
HAZWOPER training and familiarity with safe work practices in potentially hazardous environments.
Experience with EPA Superfund projects or similar large-scale environmental remediation programs.
Strong experience in environmental remediation and site assessment, including soil and groundwater investigations.
Proficiency in conducting remedial investigations and developing corrective action strategies for contaminated sites, including UST corrective actions.
Knowledge of environmental compliance requirements and regulatory frameworks relevant to EPA, Superfund, and state programs.
Understanding of hydrogeology and the ability to evaluate groundwater conditions and contaminant transport.
Ability to perform data evaluation and statistical analysis to support risk assessments and remedial decision-making.
Bachelors degree in Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Professional Engineer (PE) or Professional Geologist (PG) certification preferred.
Experience working on projects under Delaware HSCA and Brownfields programs and EPA Region III initiatives.
Experience in environmental science, geology, and hydrogeology applied to contaminated site investigations.
Experience with brownfield redevelopment projects and associated regulatory and technical requirements.
Familiarity with environmental compliance processes, including documentation, reporting, and interaction with regulatory agencies.
Ability to develop focused planning documents using data quality objectives to guide project scope and data collection.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical writing skills to communicate complex environmental findings clearly.
Demonstrated versatility and ability to work effectively within a small, close-knit project team.

Work Environment

You will work in a small, quiet office environment that values teamwork, versatility, and close collaboration, typically with 35 people present in the office. Standard working hours are 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The role offers the potential for up to one day per week of remote work for qualified candidates. Projects are primarily government-funded through EPA programs, providing a stable, recession-resistant workload. The firm emphasizes a supportive culture where team members contribute across multiple aspects of environmental projects and benefit from competitive paid time off and a professional, focused atmosphere.

Job Type & Location

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Newark, DE.

Pay And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $43.00 - $58.00/hr.

Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors.

Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific elections, plan, or program terms. If eligible, the benefits available for this temporary role may include the following: Medical, dental & vision Critical Illness, Accident, and Hospital 401(k) Retirement Plan Pre-tax and Roth post-tax contributions available Life Insurance (Voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependents) Short and long-term disability Health Spending Account (HSA) Transportation benefits Employee Assistance Program Time Off/Leave (PTO, Vacation or Sick Leave)

Workplace Type

This is a hybrid position in Newark,DE.

Application Deadline

This position is anticipated to close on Oct 19, 2026.

About Actalent

Actalent is a global leader in engineering and sciences services and talent solutions. We help visionary companies advance their engineering and science initiatives through access to specialized experts who drive scale, innovation and speed to market. With a network of almost 20,000 consultants and 5,000 clients across the U.S., Canada, Asia and Europe, Actalent serves many of the Fortune 500. We are proud to be an Engineering News-Record (ENR) Top 500 Design Firm for our engineering design services and a ClearlyRated Best of Staffing® winner for both client and talent service.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
U.S. Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officers diligently work to safeguard our nation’s heroes and their families from health hazards.

As a professional in the environmental science or environmental engineer field, a career as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer might be one for you.

Outstanding Benefits and Opportunities

As an Environmental Science / Engineering Officer for the U.S. Army, you will identify and evaluate potential health risks and develop a course of action to control or prevent disease, illness, and injury. You may supervise the scientific research for environmental health and industrial hygiene, assess weapons, equipment, clothing, and material systems, and develop policies, programs, and operations to ensure the health and safety of Soldiers and staff. You will attend trainings, continued education programs, seminars, and conferences to broaden your knowledge base, collaborate with other top professionals and interact with the newest technologies in the field.

If you choose to join the Army Reserve, you will be able to serve your country as needed while still supporting your community.

Regardless of how you choose to serve, a career as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer allows you to be all you can be.

Outstanding Benefits and Opportunities

When you join the Army Medical Service Corps, you’ll be making a difference in the lives of our Soldiers and the country at large while gaining access to invaluable opportunities, like supporting humanitarian missions, being part of a dedicated healthcare team, and leadership training, all while earning a competitive benefits package.

Benefits may include:
★ Repayment of qualified education loans to lending institution, paid annually over a maximum of 3 years while serving
★ Based on your field of concentration, you may be eligible for an accession bonus
★ Travel opportunities within the United States and abroad
★ Up to 30 days of paid vacation earned annually
★ Enrollment into the Uniformed Services Blended Retirement System
★ No- to low-cost medical and dental care for you and your family
★ Commissary and post exchange shopping privileges
★ Specialized training to become a leader in medicine

Eligibility Requirements

★ Must have a bachelor’s degree from an educational program accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health with a major in a public-health-relevant field or a bachelor’s degree from a program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology with a major in an environmental engineering-relevant field
★ Must be a U.S. citizen to serve Active Duty
★ Must have a permanent U.S. residency for Army Reserve

Have questions or want more information?

To find out more information about becoming an Environmental Science / Engineering Officer in the U.S. Army, visit www.goarmy.com/medicine. You may also contact your local Army Healthcare Recruiter to learn how you can get started on your journey as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer.

– Fortune 500 company. 100+ years in business. Leading midstream service provider. Safety first. Sustainable operations. Environmentally responsible. Employee focused.

Job Summary

Role focus is on environmental support of construction and maintenance efforts with significant work within natural and cultural resource compliance. Major work activities include but are not limited to: desktop analysis, permit applicability review, agency interactions, management of 3rd party resource experts, construction compliance planning, field compliance inspections, project restoration, and close out requirements. Job Profile Summary

Responsible for coordinating environmental compliance, remediation and company support for operating segments and construction projects through the application of knowledge and experience of compliance and environmental programs in accordance with the company mission, vision, and values.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Provide mentoring to entry level employees on compliance system management, assisting with compliance requirements and organizational procedures and tools.
Develop tools and templates to manage the collection of environmental compliance and remediation information that results in enhanced compliance and company performance with the appropriate quality and accuracy reviews of the data.
Manage field inspections for operating assets and construction projects. Provide senior level knowledge of compliance requirements and operating or construction parameters to answer questions regarding applicability and compliance requirements.
Enhance existing compliance programs based on audit results. Lead internal audits of facilities within and outside areas of responsibility.
Represent the company in the evaluation and implementation of minor emerging regulatory issues through committees of state based Industry Associations or in support of the company's Regulatory Issue Guideline.
Recognize and resolve regulatory applicability issues and identify compliance requirements and tasks. Able to apply risk based analysis of compliance related to operations or construction practices. Provide support to less experienced professionals to resolve complex questions of applicability or requirements.
Capable of managing all environmental programs and their application within a complex operating asset or construction projects.
Recognize the need for and development of new procedures and tools to facilitate and demonstrate compliance.
Review environmental inspection reports and resolve potential compliance issues based on knowledge of regulations, construction practices and operating assets.
Negotiate with contract and consultant resources to ensure an appropriate level of service and competitive rates for service are in place. Evaluate contractor and consultant performance and make recommendations on continued use.
Manage the permit process from start to finish for all media, including applications for new construction and operating assets. Ensure quality and accuracy of practical permit conditions based on evaluation of compliance risk.
Manage multiple compliance systems across multiple media for complex operating sites and projects. Contribute to system enhancements to improve compliance performance. Train new users on compliance systems and procedures. Participate in the development and implementation of new compliance systems.
Manage and participate in agency inspections and represent the company in negotiations on compliance or enforcement issues. Effectively represent the company operating parameters and construction practices and the applicability of environmental regulations along with rationale for compliance positions taken by the organization.
Coordinate and facilitate environmental project permitting prior to, during, and after construction for maintenance, growth and large capital projects.
Collect and review environmental field samples (air, water, and waste) for analysis.

Ability to: evaluate, research, and interpret governmental regulations, equipment performance manuals, regulatory agency guidance and instructions, reports, correspondence, and company policies and procedures.
Ability to: pay attention to details.
Ability to: apply math, algebraic formulas, and statistics.
Ability to: interact, advise and communicate effectively, exchange information/provide instructions, conduct verbal presentations.
Ability to: develop communications utilizing fundamental technical writing skills.
Ability to: present training materials.
Ability to: utilize office equipment including computers and applicable job related software, including Microsoft Office tools.
Ability to: operate tools/equipment.

Weston is hiring a Senior Project Scientist to support environmental investigation, remediation, and emergency response projects that protect public health and the environment. This role is ideal for an experienced technical leader who can manage complex field efforts, guide technical decisions, and deliver high-quality client outcomes.

Lead complex environmental investigations, remediation programs, emergency response activities, and related field and office assignments from planning through completion.

Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager American Peat Technology (APT) is seeking a Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager to lead and maintain our quality control, product regulatory compliance, environmental permitting, and product registration programs.
This is a hands-on, technical position supporting APT’s manufacturing of granular peat products, microbial inoculants, turf products, fertilizers, soil amendments, and other agricultural products sold throughout the United States and Canada.
The position combines laboratory testing, manufacturing quality control, regulatory affairs, environmental compliance, product registrations, and new product commercialization. This individual will have significant ownership and authority for APT’s quality, regulatory, and environmental compliance programs and will directly supervise the Lab Manager.
The position works closely with R&D, Production, Sales, the Safety Coordinator, management, regulatory agencies, consultants, outside laboratories, and other internal and external partners.
Key Responsibilities Quality Control & Product Quality

Lead and maintain APT’s quality-control program, including testing methods, product specifications, acceptance standards, and finished-product release criteria.
Oversee quality testing of raw materials, in-process materials, and finished products, including applicable moisture, particle size, bulk density, pH, ash, nutrient, microbial, heavy metals, and other product testing.
Provide direction and oversight to the Lab Manager and support effective laboratory operations, documentation, equipment, training, and testing priorities.
Evaluate testing data, investigate unexpected results and nonconformances, and coordinate corrective actions.
Exercise appropriate authority to hold or prevent the release of materials or products that do not meet established quality requirements.

Product Regulatory Affairs & Registrations

Own and maintain APT’s product registration program for products sold throughout the United States and Canada.
Research and interpret requirements for fertilizers, soil amendments, microbial and biological products, turf products, and other agricultural products.
Manage registrations, renewals, amendments, fees, reports, and required supporting documentation.
Review product labels, claims, guaranteed analyses, and supporting materials for regulatory compliance.
Monitor regulatory changes and coordinate responses to regulatory agency questions and requests.

Environmental Permitting & Compliance

Own environmental compliance for APT’s Minnesota manufacturing operations, including applicable state and federal permits and regulatory requirements.
Prepare and coordinate permit applications, renewals, modifications, reports, monitoring information, and other required documentation.
Monitor operations for compliance and maintain accurate, audit-ready records.
Serve as a primary contact for environmental regulatory agencies and coordinate with outside consultants and technical resources.
Support regulatory inspections, audits, investigations, and corrective actions.

New Product Development & Commercialization

Partner with R&D, Sales, Production, and other departments to identify regulatory, registration, labeling, testing, and quality requirements for new products.
Establish product specifications, QC requirements, acceptance standards, and finished-product release criteria.
Coordinate required product registrations and approvals prior to commercial sale.
Review proposed labels, claims, formulations, raw materials, and product or process changes for regulatory and quality impacts.
Maintain and continuously improve APT’s regulatory and quality-control commercialization sign-off process.

Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and technical reasoning skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Ability to independently research, interpret, and apply technical procedures and regulatory requirements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external partners.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn applicable laboratory, quality, regulatory, and business systems.

About FIU

Florida International University is a Top 50, preeminent public research university with 55,000 students from all 50 states and more than 140 countries, as well as an alumni network of more than 340,000. Located in the global city of Miami, the university offers more than 200 degree programs at the undergraduate, graduate and professional levels, including medicine and law. A Carnegie R1 institution, FIU drives impactful research in environmental resilience, health and technology and innovation. Home to the Wall of Wind and Institute of Environment, FIU stands at the forefront of discovery and innovation. With a focus on student success, economic mobility and community engagement, FIU is redefining what it means to be a public research university.

Tenure Track Assistant Professor and Associate Professor in Environmental Health Sciences

The Robert Stempel College Of Public Health & Social Work At Florida International University (FIU) Invites Applications For Two Full-time, Tenure-earning/tenure-track Faculty Positions In The Department Of Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) Under Two Main Concentrations:

Assistant Professor (Tenure Track) ' Environmental Health Sciences (EHS)
Assistant/Associate Professor (Tenure Track or Tenured) ' Brain, Behavior, and the Environment (BBE)

The College also ranks 15th in NIH funding among public universities (Blue Ridge Institute for Medical Research). Located in Miami'a vibrant global hub near world-renowned beaches and the Florida Keys'Stempel College offers an exceptional setting for impactful public health research and education. To learn more about Stempel College, please refer to our 2025 Impact Report.

We seek energetic, visionary scholars whose research advances understanding of how environmental exposures shape human health. Desired areas of expertise include environmental health sciences, carcinogenesis, environmental toxicology, precision environmental health, and neurotoxicology (Assistant Professor, EHS), as well as environmental neuroscience or neurotoxicology examining the impacts of pollutants on brain health, behavior, and neurological outcomes (Assistant/Associate Professor, BBE).

Occupational and Environmental epidemiology

, in collaboration with the departments of Psychology at FIU.
