new_jobs.description:
Description

At Weston Solutions, Inc. you will do meaningful work and make valuable contributions. Employee ownership at Weston is a path to professional growth and access to diverse opportunities in a highly connected community that works together across key service areas to make a difference in the environment. Weston has continued to evolve and adapt to our changing world as a premier provider of environmental and infrastructure services for over sixty years. In both the public and private sectors our teams help identify, solve, mitigate, and manage critical environmental issues to help clients achieve a more sustainable future.

Weston is hiring a Senior Project Scientist to support environmental investigation, remediation, and emergency response projects that protect public health and the environment. This role is ideal for an experienced technical leader who can manage complex field efforts, guide technical decisions, and deliver high-quality client outcomes.

This position supports a critical project with work expected to begin soon. Weston is proactively interviewing to prepare for onboarding as project activities ramp up. Start timing will align with project kickoff and mobilization schedules.

Location: Pittsburgh, PA

Key Responsibilities

Lead complex environmental investigations, remediation programs, emergency response activities, and related field and office assignments from planning through completion.
Manage project execution in accordance with scope, budget, schedule, technical requirements, regulatory standards, Weston procedures, and client expectations.
Plan and oversee field investigations and sampling programs at active construction, remediation, and potentially hazardous sites.
Direct field staff, subcontractors, and multidisciplinary teams while coordinating resources and reinforcing safe, efficient work practices.
Analyze field observations, analytical data, and monitoring results to develop defensible conclusions, recommendations, and project strategies.
Prepare and review scientific reports, investigation summaries, removal action documentation, technical memoranda, work plans, sampling plans, health and safety plans, quality assurance documents, schedules, budgets, and other deliverables.
Conduct peer reviews of project scopes, technical documents, calculations, data interpretations, and deliverables to support quality and consistency.
Identify project risks, constraints, and opportunities, and implement corrective actions when needed.
Communicate project objectives, progress, needs, concerns, and deliverable expectations to clients, stakeholders, Project Managers, subcontractors, technical teams, and leadership.
Maintain accurate and auditable field documentation, correspondence, notebooks, technical files, and project records.
Mentor junior staff and provide technical guidance to project teams.
Evaluate new technologies, tools, and techniques for potential use in project execution and Weston service offerings.

Safety Responsibilities

Lead EHS compliance for complex assignments and ensure work aligns with Weston’s EHS Program, project safety plans, technical procedures, quality requirements, and applicable regulations.
Reinforce Stop Work Authority, personal accountability, and project- and site-specific safety expectations with staff and subcontractors.
Coordinate with EHS personnel when plans do not align with project scope or site conditions.
Work safely at active and potentially hazardous sites using required PPE, including OSHA Levels D through A, as applicable.

Required Qualifications:

10 to 15 years of relevant experience in environmental investigations, remediation, emergency response operations, or a combination of these areas.
This position requires U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in environmental science, Geoscience, Engineering, Physical Science, Life Science, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading complex environmental site investigations or remediation projects involving potentially hazardous substances.
Ability to serve as a technical resource, guide complex technical decisions, solve problems, and manage multiple priorities.
Experience managing field operations, subcontractors, multidisciplinary teams, project scope, schedules, budgets, resources, risks, and technical deliverables.
Experience developing and reviewing technical reports, investigation documents, work plans, field sampling plans, health and safety plans, technical procedures, and quality assurance documentation.
Strong ability to analyze, interpret, organize, and communicate analytical data, monitoring results, and field observations.
Strong leadership, mentoring, client-facing, written, and verbal communication skills.
Experience using field sampling equipment, air and water monitoring instruments, PPE, and related field tools.
Valid driver’s license.

Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910, or willingness to obtain it.
Incident Command System training or emergency response experience.
Experience with QAPPs or UFP QAPPs.
Membership in a relevant professional organization.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and standard business communication tools.

Travel, On-Call, and Physical Requirements

Willingness to travel, complete extended field assignments, and mobilize rapidly for project or emergency response needs.
Ability to participate in on-call rotations and support 24/7 responses to environmental incidents, including chemical and oil spills.
Ability to work outdoors at active construction, investigation, and remediation sites.
Ability to walk long distances over varied terrain, climb ladders, work at elevation, and lift and carry up to 50 pounds, including field equipment and PPE.

new_jobs.title: Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager
new_jobs.description:
Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager American Peat Technology (APT) is seeking a Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager to lead and maintain our quality control, product regulatory compliance, environmental permitting, and product registration programs.
This is a hands-on, technical position supporting APT’s manufacturing of granular peat products, microbial inoculants, turf products, fertilizers, soil amendments, and other agricultural products sold throughout the United States and Canada.
The position combines laboratory testing, manufacturing quality control, regulatory affairs, environmental compliance, product registrations, and new product commercialization. This individual will have significant ownership and authority for APT’s quality, regulatory, and environmental compliance programs and will directly supervise the Lab Manager.
The position works closely with R&D, Production, Sales, the Safety Coordinator, management, regulatory agencies, consultants, outside laboratories, and other internal and external partners.
Key Responsibilities Quality Control & Product Quality

Lead and maintain APT’s quality-control program, including testing methods, product specifications, acceptance standards, and finished-product release criteria.
Oversee quality testing of raw materials, in-process materials, and finished products, including applicable moisture, particle size, bulk density, pH, ash, nutrient, microbial, heavy metals, and other product testing.
Provide direction and oversight to the Lab Manager and support effective laboratory operations, documentation, equipment, training, and testing priorities.
Evaluate testing data, investigate unexpected results and nonconformances, and coordinate corrective actions.
Exercise appropriate authority to hold or prevent the release of materials or products that do not meet established quality requirements.

Product Regulatory Affairs & Registrations

Own and maintain APT’s product registration program for products sold throughout the United States and Canada.
Research and interpret requirements for fertilizers, soil amendments, microbial and biological products, turf products, and other agricultural products.
Manage registrations, renewals, amendments, fees, reports, and required supporting documentation.
Review product labels, claims, guaranteed analyses, and supporting materials for regulatory compliance.
Monitor regulatory changes and coordinate responses to regulatory agency questions and requests.

Environmental Permitting & Compliance

Own environmental compliance for APT’s Minnesota manufacturing operations, including applicable state and federal permits and regulatory requirements.
Prepare and coordinate permit applications, renewals, modifications, reports, monitoring information, and other required documentation.
Monitor operations for compliance and maintain accurate, audit-ready records.
Serve as a primary contact for environmental regulatory agencies and coordinate with outside consultants and technical resources.
Support regulatory inspections, audits, investigations, and corrective actions.

New Product Development & Commercialization

Partner with R&D, Sales, Production, and other departments to identify regulatory, registration, labeling, testing, and quality requirements for new products.
Establish product specifications, QC requirements, acceptance standards, and finished-product release criteria.
Coordinate required product registrations and approvals prior to commercial sale.
Review proposed labels, claims, formulations, raw materials, and product or process changes for regulatory and quality impacts.
Maintain and continuously improve APT’s regulatory and quality-control commercialization sign-off process.

What We’re Looking For Associate degree in a scientific, technical, environmental, agricultural, microbiological, chemistry, or related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience.
Previous experience in quality control, manufacturing, environmental compliance, regulatory affairs, laboratory operations, or a related technical field preferred.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and technical reasoning skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Ability to independently research, interpret, and apply technical procedures and regulatory requirements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external partners.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn applicable laboratory, quality, regulatory, and business systems.
Experience with agricultural product registrations, microbiology, qPCR, product labeling, laboratory method development, or manufacturing process improvement is preferred.

Core Competencies We are looking for someone who demonstrates attention to detail, analytical thinking, problem solving, ownership and accountability, people leadership, organization and planning, sound judgment, effective communication, collaboration, and emotional intelligence.
Schedule & Location This position is generally Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with occasional additional days or hours as needed.
Work locations include APT’s main plant in Spencer Township, APT2, and the Applied Research Center in Aitkin, Minnesota.
This position reports to the VP of Business Development and works closely with other members of the R&D team.

Paid time off (PTO)
Medical, dental and vision plans
Matching 401(k)
Life Insurance
Paid volunteer opportunities

new_jobs.description:
ERM
is seeking a Technical Partner
to help grow our Natural Resources practice, with a focus on supporting power, renewable energy, diversified energy, and technology sector clients across North America.

Location: this is a hybrid role and can be based out of any of our offices across the USA

This role will provide technical leadership in biological resources, ecological mitigation, habitat conservation, ecological restoration, and environmental permitting. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to clients developing and operating major infrastructure projects while helping expand ERM's market presence and technical capabilities.

As a Partner, you will combine technical expertise, client relationship management, and business leadership to build long-term client partnerships, develop new business opportunities, and mentor multidisciplinary teams. This is an opportunity to join ERM's global partnership and play a leading role in delivering complex environmental solutions for some of North America's most significant energy and infrastructure projects.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will:

Lead business development and client engagement activities within the Power, Diversified Energy, and Technology sectors.
Provide senior technical leadership for biological resources, ecological restoration, habitat conservation, and environmental permitting programs.
Support clients through project planning, permitting, construction, and operations phases.
Develop and grow key client relationships while identifying opportunities for additional services.
Mentor and develop technical staff and project managers.
Collaborate with ERM partners and service line leaders to support regional and national growth initiatives.
Drive project delivery excellence while meeting financial, safety, and quality objectives.

What You'll Bring

Required:

BS/MS in environmental science, engineering, or related field.
15+ years of progressive experience in environmental consulting.
Proven leadership in mitigation and ecorestoration, including endangered species and habitat conservation.
Deep understanding of conventional and renewable energy markets in North America.
Strong business development track record, generating and delivering multi-million-dollar programs.
Expertise in HCPs, and regional permitting.

Preferred:

Experience establishing mitigation banks and writing vegetation management plans.
Existing client relationships in the Power, Diversified energy and/or Technology sector that can be leveraged for growth.
Familiarity with utility commissions, regulatory agencies, and emerging sustainability trends.

Why ERM?

Equity Ownership: Be a shareholder in a purpose-driven, global firm.
Strategic Influence: Shape the direction of ERM and the future of sustainable infrastructure.
Thought Leadership: Lead conversations that matter in energy, ecology, and sustainability.
Global Reach, Local Impact: Leverage ERM’s platform to amplify your influence and deliver measurable results.

Application
s accepted through September 30, 2026
.

For the Technical Partner, Natural Resources
position, the anticipated annual base pay is $175,000–$202,300 (USD)
. Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, parental leave, medical, dental, vision, life, disability, AD&D insurance, 401(k) or RRSP/DPSP, and other applicable benefits to eligible employees.

Note
: Bonuses, commissions, and other forms of additional compensation are not guaranteed and subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures.

Who We Are:

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!

#WeAreONEOK
– Fortune 500 company. 100+ years in business. Leading midstream service provider. Safety first. Sustainable operations. Environmentally responsible. Employee focused.

Job Summary

Role focus is on environmental support of construction and maintenance efforts with significant work within natural and cultural resource compliance. Major work activities include but are not limited to: desktop analysis, permit applicability review, agency interactions, management of 3rd party resource experts, construction compliance planning, field compliance inspections, project restoration, and close out requirements. Job Profile Summary

Responsible for coordinating environmental compliance, remediation and company support for operating segments and construction projects through the application of knowledge and experience of compliance and environmental programs in accordance with the company mission, vision, and values.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Provide mentoring to entry level employees on compliance system management, assisting with compliance requirements and organizational procedures and tools.
Develop tools and templates to manage the collection of environmental compliance and remediation information that results in enhanced compliance and company performance with the appropriate quality and accuracy reviews of the data.
Manage field inspections for operating assets and construction projects. Provide senior level knowledge of compliance requirements and operating or construction parameters to answer questions regarding applicability and compliance requirements.
Enhance existing compliance programs based on audit results. Lead internal audits of facilities within and outside areas of responsibility.
Represent the company in the evaluation and implementation of minor emerging regulatory issues through committees of state based Industry Associations or in support of the company's Regulatory Issue Guideline.
Recognize and resolve regulatory applicability issues and identify compliance requirements and tasks. Able to apply risk based analysis of compliance related to operations or construction practices. Provide support to less experienced professionals to resolve complex questions of applicability or requirements.
Capable of managing all environmental programs and their application within a complex operating asset or construction projects.
Recognize the need for and development of new procedures and tools to facilitate and demonstrate compliance.
Review environmental inspection reports and resolve potential compliance issues based on knowledge of regulations, construction practices and operating assets.
Negotiate with contract and consultant resources to ensure an appropriate level of service and competitive rates for service are in place. Evaluate contractor and consultant performance and make recommendations on continued use.
Manage the permit process from start to finish for all media, including applications for new construction and operating assets. Ensure quality and accuracy of practical permit conditions based on evaluation of compliance risk.
Manage multiple compliance systems across multiple media for complex operating sites and projects. Contribute to system enhancements to improve compliance performance. Train new users on compliance systems and procedures. Participate in the development and implementation of new compliance systems.
Manage and participate in agency inspections and represent the company in negotiations on compliance or enforcement issues. Effectively represent the company operating parameters and construction practices and the applicability of environmental regulations along with rationale for compliance positions taken by the organization.
Coordinate and facilitate environmental project permitting prior to, during, and after construction for maintenance, growth and large capital projects.
Collect and review environmental field samples (air, water, and waste) for analysis.

Education

Bachelor's Degree in environmental, natural science, engineering preferred and/or a combination of formal education and the following job related experience:

Work Experience

This role is typically attained through 6 -10 years related experience in environmental compliance.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of: state and federal environmental regulations and standards and their applicability to operations.
Ability to: analyze, research, compile, and prepare permit applications, logs, reports, and correspondence and company responses to agency requests.
Ability to: evaluate, research, and interpret governmental regulations, equipment performance manuals, regulatory agency guidance and instructions, reports, correspondence, and company policies and procedures.
Ability to: pay attention to details.
Ability to: apply math, algebraic formulas, and statistics.
Ability to: interact, advise and communicate effectively, exchange information/provide instructions, conduct verbal presentations.
Ability to: develop communications utilizing fundamental technical writing skills.
Ability to: present training materials.
Ability to: utilize office equipment including computers and applicable job related software, including Microsoft Office tools.
Ability to: operate tools/equipment.

Licenses and Certifications

None required

Strength Factor Rating - Physical Demands/Requirements

Sedentary Work - Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally (Occasionally: activity or condition exists up to 1/3 of the time) and/or a negligible amount of force frequently (Frequently: activity or condition exists from 1/3 to 2/3 of the time) to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time, but may involve walking or standing for brief periods of time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met.

Sitting: Remaining in a seated position (Constantly)

Kneeling: Bending the legs at the knees to come to rest on the knee or knees (Occasionally)
Crouching: Bending the body downward and forward by bending the legs and spine (Occasionally)
Crawling: Moving about on the hands and arms in any direction (Occasionally)
Reaching: Extending hands and arms in any direction (Constantly)
Handling: Seizing, holding, grasping, turning or otherwise working with the hand or hands (Manual Dexterity) (Constantly)
Fingering: Picking, pinching or otherwise working with the fingers primarily (Finger Dexterity) (Constantly)
Feeling: Perceiving such attributes of objects/materials as size, shape, temperature, texture, movement or pulsation by receptors in the skin, particularly those of the finger tips (Constantly)

Tasting/Smelling: (Occasionally)

Far Vision: Clarity of vision at 20 feet for more (Frequently)
Depth Perception: Three-dimensional vision; ability to judge distances and spatial relationships so as to see objects where and as they actually are (Frequently)
Vision: Color - The ability to identify and distinguish colors (Constantly)

new_jobs.title: Associate Director - Ecology
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

Are you ready to join a team of talented Ecologist’s and shape the future of the environment?

Join our dynamic Nature team as a Associate Ecologist in our UK including Manchester, Leeds, Basingstoke, Newcastle, Croydon, Birmingham, Cambridge, Nottingham and Liverpool offices (other locations across the UK may be considered). Our Nature team are working on a mix of large infrastructure projects in the energy, water, renewables, defence and transport sectors, alongside managing smaller local projects. Our team is also supporting the wider AECOM Nature team with National and International projects.

In this role, depending on your interests and skillset, you will have opportunities to support on a variety of areas such as: using innovative survey techniques for species and habitats surveys, data capture and reporting; work winning; management of projects, Habitats Regulations Assessments; and Biodiversity Net Gain mentoring and coaching of the team. Our supportive environment offers both internal and external training opportunities within a nurturing mentoring and coaching framework.

Here’s what you’ll do:

Lead the planning and delivery of ecological inputs for both internal and external clients ;
Produce and technically review a range of ecological assessments including Preliminary Ecological Appraisal; Protected Species Baseline Reports; Ecological Impact Assessments; Habitats Regulations Assessment; and Biodiversity Net Gain Calculations;
Provide technical leadership to support the delivery of proportionate and pragmatic solutions;
Lead consultation and engagement with clients and key project stakeholders including planning authorities, statutory bodies and the public;
Play a key role in the continued development of our technical capabilities and encourage the embedding of innovation/research;
Lead the production of bids and tenders for ecological services;
Mentor and support both junior staff and peers.

If you're passionate about innovation and turning bold ideas into reality, AECOM welcomes you. Join our team, where we don't just construct infrastructure but also uplift communities and enhance lives. Why not give our AECOM page on LinkedIn a follow to stay updated on the impactful projects we're working on and see firsthand the difference we're making in the industry!

Come grow with us.
